subject: general
question:
Study the figures A and B carefully. What is the reason for the increase in volume in dough B?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbe456220d83bc56b807b3c279086ea8e8a405eb8b589d24f68ae31a5df856ac.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/097d7d1291e3689ea501f0c529f4d79e0febd9f8890403407e3792f5e74a0a6a.png]

options.text: Alcohol is produced that increases the volume
Lactic acid is produced that increases the volume
CO₂ produced during respiration increases the volume
Water is produced that increases the volume

solution:
The correct answer is __**CO2 produced during respiration increases the volume**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CO₂ **is a by-product of cellular **respiration **in living organisms.
 
• CO₂ produced during respiration increases the **volume of air in the lungs**, this is known as **hyperventilation**.
 
• **Hyperventilation **occurs when an individual breathes faster or deeper than normal.
 
• **Hyperventilation **can lead to a decrease in the amount of** CO2 in the blood.**
 
• This decrease in CO2 can cause symptoms such as **lightheadedness.**
 
• Hyperventilation can also cause other symptoms** such as tingling in the fingers and mouth, muscle spasms, and shortness of breath.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• During normal breathing, carbon dioxide (CO₂) is produced as **a waste product of metabolism.**
 
• CO2 is carried by the blood to the lungs, where it is **exhaled**.
 
• In the lungs,** CO2 acts as a respiratory stimulant**, which helps to regulate the rate and depth of breathing.
 
• The CO2 level in the blood is closely regulated to maintain a balance between **the amount produced and the amount exhaled.**
 
• When the level of CO2 in the blood is too high, it can cause an increase in the **volume of air in the lungs**, which is known as **hyperventilation**.
 
• **Hyperventilation **can also be caused by** anxiety, panic attacks, and other emotional disturbances.**
 
• Hyperventilation can be treated by various methods,** such as breathing exercises, to help regulate the breathing rate and decrease the volume of air in the lungs.**
